clue.text: Cross the royal mail must bear

definitions.text: Cross the royal mail must bear

parts.words: Cross the royal mail must bear
parts.note: a ballot-paper cross sent through the post by an absent voter is a letter the Royal Mail has to carry

explanation.surface: An irritable member of the royal household is someone the post office staff must put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry and 'the royal' a person; really the cross is the mark on a ballot paper, and Royal Mail is Britain's postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot cast by post rather than in person is carried by the mail service to the count.

clue.text: To chat up chasing love is fine

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for chat is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to yak is to chat idly

explanation.surface: Flirting with someone after falling for them is perfectly all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To chat up' reads like flirting, but in a down clue 'up' reverses the word for chat, and 'chasing' places it after love.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal ways of saying something is acceptable or all right.

clue.text: Walk unsteadily and let fly, drinking rum

indicators.note: drinking means taking something inside, so one piece holds the other
to let fly is to throw wildly, so the letters of let are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
rum in its old sense of strange means odd

explanation.surface: Someone staggers and lashes out after too much rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' scrambles the three letters of let to TLE. 'Rum' looks like the drink but is the old British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child's first steps are tottering and unsteady, which is how one is said to move.

clue.text: Globes that are only round bulbous shapes to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: A definition of globes as nothing more than round, bulbous forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres are called globes, and these are the round balls of royal regalia or the heavens.

clue.text: Transport it alone?

indicators.note: transport means carry off or move about, so the letters of it alone are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether you can carry something by yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' is both the anagram signal and, in its sense of rapture, the meaning: joy so great it carries you away on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A transport of joy is an older phrase for being overcome with delight or rapture.

clue.text: Buffer to apply to Oxford

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe, and a buffer here is something used to shine it

explanation.surface: Something to cushion or shield the university town of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the city or university, but an Oxford is a lace-up shoe; buffer means something you buff with, not a cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax or cream rubbed onto leather footwear to buff it to a shine.

clue.text: Returns drinks and stumbles

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
to trip is to stumble

explanation.surface: Someone comes back from the pub having had several drinks and falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, buying a round means paying for drinks for everyone in your group.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeys out and back again, as with return tickets, are also called returns.

clue.text: Get away from fire (almost)

indicators.note: almost means the word for fire loses its final letter

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: An instruction to move away from a blaze, if only nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from SHOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation used to drive off an animal or person, telling them to be off.

clue.text: Light workout — land a brace!

indicators.note: a workout puts the letters of land a brace through their paces into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gentle exercise session in which you manage to win two of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective describing the workout, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A branched holder for several candles is a source of illumination in a room.

clue.text: Young men accept northern nations

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the word for young men holds the other letter

parts.note: lads are young men

explanation.surface: Young men are welcoming northerners among nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Countries are also called lands, as in the phrase foreign lands.

clue.text: Serving dish bearing signature engraved in it

indicators.note: bearing means carrying within, so the letters sit across signature engraved

explanation.surface: A dish for serving food has the maker's mark engraved into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of signature and the start of engraved; 'in it' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep lidded bowl from which soup is ladled at the table.

clue.text: TV programme with which the day closes

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday, a day of the week
closes in the sense of finishes means ends

explanation.surface: Naming a television show that is broadcast as the day comes to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: The day meant is Friday, written in its short form FRI.
explanation.definitionFit: An American sitcom about six young New Yorkers, one of the most famous shows on television.

clue.text: Beginning to doubt?

parts.note: read as a beginning that is doubtful, a start in a race that does not count because someone moved too soon

explanation.surface: Someone is starting to have doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a start whose validity is in doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: When a runner leaves before the gun, the race is recalled, so that opening was bogus.

clue.text: Makeshift process — oversimplified file extracted

indicators.note: process means work over, so the letters of oversimplified are rearranged once the letters of file are taken away

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready method arises when an over-simple document is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted' tells us to remove the letters of FILE from OVERSIMPLIFIED; 'process' rearranges the remaining OVRSMPIIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigged up from whatever is to hand is put together on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Spread out and quietly go in to kill

indicators.note: go in means the letter for quietly enters the word for kill

parts.note: to slay is to kill
p (piano) is the musical instruction for quietly

explanation.surface: An instruction to fan out and creep in silently for the kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To splay limbs or fingers is to stretch them apart widely.

clue.text: Associate of a right wing type

parts.note: Con is the short form of Conservative, the right-wing party in Britain
a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Someone is a friend of a right-wing kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or companion, especially the spouse of a reigning monarch, is a companion in the sense of associate.

clue.text: The impact of money is about right

indicators.note: is about means the word for money surrounds the letter

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A remark that money's effect really concerns what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places R inside CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision is a violent impact, as in a car smash.

clue.text: Reject encouragement and direction

parts.note: a spur is an incentive or encouragement
N for north is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Turning down both a motivation and a course to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn an offer is to scornfully refuse it.

clue.text: An easy runner might look at exercises

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
PE stands for physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A relaxed jogger might glance at the exercise programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: an easy runner might lope, moving with long relaxed strides.
explanation.definitionFit: A long relaxed bounding stride is how a runner covers ground without hurrying.

clue.text: Car gets back home following the road

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the motorway letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first main motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: back means the word for home is read backwards

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A car returns home after a journey along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for home. 'the road' is the M1, Britain's motorway from London to Leeds, which crosswords write with the letter I for the figure one.
explanation.definitionFit: A small British-made motor, iconic since the 1960s, is a model of car.

clue.text: Sarah's got a sauce!

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of Sarah, so Sarah's becomes Sal's

explanation.surface: Sarah has picked up some kind of sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' could also mean cheek, but here it is the spicy dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy tomato-based Latin American relish, often served with tortilla chips.

clue.text: Afflicted by sulphur on glove

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a mitten is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: Something has been tainted by sulphur on a glove.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck down by illness or misfortune is an old sense; smitten is the past participle of smite.

clue.text: Anger found in modern day broadcast

indicators.note: found in means the word for anger sits inside the other letters

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the modern era of dates
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury is detected in a programme broadcast recently.
explanation.definitionFit: A show that has been transmitted on radio or television has gone out on air.

clue.text: Come on pitch and start yelling for efficiency

indicators.note: pitch means throw, so the letters of come on are tossed into a new order
start tells us to take the opening letter of yelling

explanation.surface: Encouragement shouted from the pitch at the start of a game in the name of efficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sports field, but it is the anagram signal, turning COME ON into ECONOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy means thrift and careful use of resources, which is efficiency.

clue.text: Gets a free ride — with problems

definitions.meaning: travels by thumbing lifts from passing drivers
snags or difficulties that hold things up

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker gets a lift but runs into trouble along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbing lifts is hitchhiking, and snags in a plan are difficulties, both from the verb meaning to fasten or catch.

clue.text: Blue cheese, or brie and Leicester to form starters

indicators.note: starters means the opening letter of each of the six words before form

explanation.surface: Choosing among cheeses, such as blue, brie or Leicester, to make an appetiser course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like part of 'blue cheese' but is the definition. Red Leicester is an English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue pigment is named after the metal used to colour glass and pottery.

clue.text: Three times doctor makes a stand!

parts.note: tri- is a prefix meaning three or three times
a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor triples his output to create a display stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged metal rest for hot pots is a stand for the kitchen table.

clue.text: Loudly taunt the supporters of course

indicators.note: loudly signals the word for taunt is to be pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: to tease is to taunt

explanation.surface: Shouting jibes at those cheering on the side, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally', but it means of a golf course: the pegs that support the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegs on which golfers set their ball for each drive hold it up on a golf course.

clue.text: Irregular deep-laid store

indicators.note: irregular means take only the odd letters of deep-laid, skipping the others

explanation.surface: An odd, carefully planned shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling cooked meats and cheeses is a delicatessen, a specialist food store.

clue.text: Make no progress in the main

definitions.text: Make no progress in the main

parts.words: Make no progress in the main
parts.note: in the main means at sea, where a swimmer can stay upright in one place without moving forward

explanation.surface: A general observation about failing to get anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'generally' but means in the sea, the main being an old word for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying afloat upright by moving the legs keeps one in place, and figuratively means marking time.

clue.text: Regrets reporting deception

indicators.note: reporting signals the word for deception as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or deception

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about exposing a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to be sorry for it, to wish it undone.

clue.text: Lining up for a title soon, potentially

indicators.note: potentially says the letters of a title soon could make something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting in position for a championship that could come shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lining up' suggests competitors, but here it means traffic queuing bumper to bumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles following closely one behind another in a queue are said to be bumper to bumper.
